notes.title: Steam Deck Native Port + Dev.Play
notes.content:
[h1]Steam Deck Native Port[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/37d5a7503a5f0f683e9fa8db954900c39fef7570.png[/img]

It'ssssssssssss here!

The game should now work properly on Linux, and of course, THE STEAM DECK!

You may be saying "Why did you port it? Didn't you say that you have no desire to work on the game anymore?". That is true, but in the meantime, I started being a full-time indie developer, which forced me to make some decisions. I decided that I would continue working on PalmRide just so I can get it in a more "final" state.

So yeah, enjoy PalmRide on the Steam Deck and any other Linux device. :) 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/ce56880777382d33dfdb34c3f67401721789cd8e.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/319cfa96940e8c5ee0510399d78b754756a1e909.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/6691d6e3ae7ddf13249af192cf824180fed6f871.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/6e20492298da0590bfb02b6e8a4f578dde3b0e16.gif[/img]

!!!! It doesn't work with Proton, you need to force it to use the native game!!!

[h1]Dev.Play[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/48cf29be197e085d0e12635541f7f9e7f1d9eccc.png[/img]

For those who don't know, Dev.Play is an Eastern European conference where game developers meet, attend workshops and talk to publishers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/bad88b6e7ac14fd83be14e898836a6317e06ff20.png[/img]

This year, the event takes place in Bucharest, so if you come, there is a good chance we'll meet.

The game is now on a 50% discount due to Dev.Play, and it is also featured on the Dev.Play sale page (you should see it on the front page of Steam). This 50% discount will last a week.

[h1]Clujotronic[/h1]

Clujotronic? Ja!
Clujotronic? Ja!

A few weeks ago, I attended Clujotronic, where PalmRide was showcased on a computer. I am thankful to everyone who played and liked the game @ Clujotronic, it was nice meeting you, guys!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/939f290a2ea2ee6ef85864f187ad9ca07c1659c3.png[/img]
(please ignore the typo, the sign should've said "PalmRide" instead of "Palm Ride")

notes.content:
The last PalmRide update is pretty minor.

Changes:

[*] Migrated the project to .NET 6 instead of .NET Core 3.1 (this shouldn't impact the game much, but if it does reveal bugs, please let me know)

notes.title: ONE YEAR ANNIVERSARY, GIVEAWAY, NEW GAME 🥳 🎊
notes.content:
[h1]The beginning[/h1]

When I was 20, I had a college course called [i]Object-Oriented Programming[/i] for which we had to make an application using C++. I made a [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/outrun/comments/fn51to/small_game_i_made_for_a_school_project_is_it/]small pseudo-3D game[/url] which I liked. I knew I wanted to make an [i]Out Run[/i]-like game with [i]Outrun[/i] aesthetics. So I started working on [i]PalmRide[/i] with my friend [b]COVALENT[/b]. After the summer of 2020, most of the mechanics of the game were already in place. 

The art was 100% done by myself. It wasn't terrible, but it wasn't great either. A guy saw [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/racinggames/comments/jhsqhx/palmride_a_synthwavestyled_driving_game/]one of my reddit posts[/url] where I would showcase the game, and he offered to redesign the car of the player. I accepted his proposal, and I let him redesign that car. The result was astonishing. I was so impressed that I proposed him to redraw all the assets of the game. At that time, only the city ([i]Shinjitsu[/i]) game map was done, so he redrew those assets. When he was done with that, we released the demo of the game which received quite some positive feedback among the people who played it. The guy I'm talking about is [b]Renegade_John[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/382e8c61dd1a953d21224e4a0b88c1a593562838.png[/img]

Until that point, the development of the game was not fast, but at least it was slow and steady. In March of 2021, the development would almost stop for various reasons. I was not only overwhelmed by the college assignments I had to do, but I was also depressed about some personal troubles. At that time, we were in the middle of the pandemic. Not leaving the house for a year had a very negative impact on me, and accentuated my depression. I was almost miserable. Working on [i]PalmRide[/i] was the last thing I was thinking about. [b]COVALENT[/b] couldn't work on the game much either. College kept him busy too. Not only that, but he was fighting with his own personal troubles too. Regarding [b]Renegade_John[/b], he just got a job at a game studio as an artist, so he had less time to work on [i]PalmRide[/i]. Not only that, but he didn't feel that confident working on a game with pixel art graphics, as that was not really his art style.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/82ee8e10960b3b512ec6a5e773773e0d8c0986d6.png[/img]

The game had to be released, so I pushed myself hard to finish the game in June 2021, as I had successfully passed all my exams. I talked to [b]Renegade_John[/b] and he agreed that he would create the remaining assets for the game in the following weeks, and so he did. After that, only me and [b]COVALENT[/b] were left to finish the game. I was still depressed at that time, so initially I didn't code that much. I pushed hard during August and September, right before the launch. Luckily, the depression started going away before launching the game (as a side note: I recommend the book [i]The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F[/i] for situations like these. Reading philosophy books also helps combat depression, but better off consult a specialist). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/39bb9b7f8cc437cd6dc4babd31630f8971520228.png[/img]

One week before launching the game, and the game was missing only one important piece. That piece was the song for the beach ([i]Ocean Drive[/i]) game map. [b]COVALENT[/b] started working on it pretty much when we started development, but he couldn't get it to sound right no matter how hard he tried. He was now rushed to finish it so we could ship the game. What ended up happening was that he completely threw away [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4HrAfODsaRo]the existing song[/url] he was working on, and started a brand new one. He stayed up all night just so he could finish the new song. The new song is the one currently in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/48b626f8fd29fff741d6b949efb852a6323324f8.png[/img]

[h1]The launch[/h1]

It's September 16 2021, [i]PalmRide[/i] gets launched. During the launch what I mostly did was share the game with [i]Discord[/i]/ [i]Reddit[/i]/ [i]Facebook[/i]/ [i]Twitter[/i]/ [i]Instagram[/i].... basically every social media platform possible. I had my posts already prepared in a [i]Google Doc[/i], all I had to do was post them, but still it took some time. Luckily, my friend [b]Taranasus[/b] helped me with some posts. He also showcased [i]PalmRide[/i] to the fans of his own game at that time, [i]Vecter[/i]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/69777248f22cd4b3c56ed08aaaf564fbf5beea28.png[/img]

A few days would go by, the feedback for the game was extremely positive, and the sales were way better than I expected. I am grateful for that. Sure, some people didn't like the game, and their reasons were perfectly valid. I noted both the positive and negative feedback, and I will use it for future games, so I know what works and what doesn't, and how things can be improved.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/906f740424f636eb5adc4ddc936e90021bb8ca34.png[/img]

The game would often crash, or take very much to load. After launch I fixed most of the crashes, and also made the game load faster. When it was initially released, the game had no controller support. A few weeks after release I would buy myself a controller and implement controller support too. We also published [url=https://www.palmride.online/episode1.html][i]Episode 1: Dreadful Diagnosis[/i][/url] on the [url=https://www.palmride.online/]official website[/url] of the game short time after. That short little story was written by [b]DabuAlexandru[/b], and polished by [b]COVALENT[/b]. Updates were going great, and everyone was happy. People enjoyed the updates that improved the game, and I enjoyed making people happy, and also the Discord engagement we had.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/f1b6947d13180c8bac9bfc5c0c14b46b3bd325dd.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/4c8155ae900647745ea3361e639127476720df6b.png[/img]

A few weeks would go by and the final year of college would begin. [i]PalmRide[/i] updates would slowly cease while I was busier and busier with assignments, deadlines, exams and working on the bachelor's thesis. Eventually, the updates would stop, as I would have less and less free time to work on the game. At that time, the pandemic was still going on, and I can't say I was enjoying that time much.

A few more months would go by and I would start being motivated to work on the game too. The planned updates were: [i]Linux[/i] port, [i]Android[/i] port, a new game map and more story episodes. I started with the [i]Linux[/i] port. I made the game compile for [i]Linux[/i], but that version was still very bad, lacking sound, crashing.... I also saw the codebase of the game for the first time in a few months and I was horrified of how bad the code was. I had no desire to continue working on that codebase so I stopped.

I few month would go by again, and I would start adding the new game map. Again, I realized that I had no desire to work on that codebase, and that I could do things better if I were to start a game from scratch.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/1cf09d008e66f5083b4d3b64784026d5573054b5.png[/img]

[h1]Rockets[/h1]

While these were happening, the last semester of college began, and I had a course called "Simulation applications programming". The subject was about making a video game which contains physics, AI and graphics programming. The game had to be made in a team. After the requirements for the game were set by the professor, I received a text message from a person, and asked me if she could join my team. I said yes, and now she was part of the team.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/1f71ee45760b981a5e09e2f6a3f7e6a456adeb15.png[/img]

The project we made was a planet lander game, where the player had to successfully land on 5 planets without hitting asteroids or landing too hard. 

That project can be found [url=https://github.com/AstroSpiders/The-Astro-Spider]here[/url].

Also, here's me presenting the game to our professor (sorry, but I speak Romanian in the video):

[previewyoutube=wqB4atBzNfA;full][/previewyoutube]

I enjoyed working on it, so I decided that it may be worth turning the prototype into a full game too. That person who joined the team for the assignment is [b]Gunter[/b]. While working on that game for college, [b]Gunter[/b] proved to be very good at designing things, choosing aesthetics, 3D modelling and presentations. I asked [b]Gunter[/b] if she would join me and [b]COVALENT[/b] in making a full game with rockets, and she said yes. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/b6d479db7d5e0c3f98750bfe0d14cc581efc26b7.png[/img]

So that's the team, me, [b]COVALENT[/b] and [b]Gunter[/b], making a new game with rockets. I can't say that much about the game, as we're very early in development, but I can at least give you some hints regarding the game. 

The game will probably feature multiple game modes:
[list]
[*] A game mode similar to [i]Vecter[/i]/ [i]PalmRide[/i] where you have to drive a spaceship endlessly
[*] A racing game mode
[*] A taxi driver game mode where you take people from one planet to another
[/list]
Style-wise, the game will probably be a low-poly with [i]Outrun[/i]/ [i]Synthwave[/i] aesthetics. There may be more dimensions, each with its own unique style, flocks of UFOs, and much, much more....

Again, the game is very early in development, and I can't know for sure what the end result will look like. What I've said here is subject to change, and things may or may not end up in the final game.

Here's what the the "game" can do so far:
[list]
[*] Rocket launching
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/31a0dd3c14c978d1dde6b9710773a097fcca9b46.gif[/img]
[*] Maneuver the rocket around a planet
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/df7e6ce2b1e27e0bce13394e23089062e0cd323b.gif[/img]
[*] Control the rocket as a spaceship when far from a planet
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/249238793c789b818609299bbe36e21c007fabca.gif[/img]
[*] And here's one rocket model prototype, made by Gunter
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/42048266fe594003ac721f41bbbe87b6fb46581b.png[/img]
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/cd2e3331db0b46824dade5b5a4b3254b2c39df07.png[/img]

It doesn't seem like much, but what we have is the foundation for the game we are making. We must make sure that the foundation is strong before actually making the game, otherwise, the development process will be very painful. Right now I'm implementing the rocket/ spaceship physics and making a system general enough that it would allow for many types of rockets, each with its own unique properties. As for the models, we're still experimenting to see what import/ export settings work, how the models should look, how the scripts should interact with them..

[h1]Giveaway[/h1]

Since PalmRide turns one year, we are giving away 10 PalmRide keys. All you have to do is join [url=https://discord.gg/NgZ3ygb8N5]our Discord server[/url], and keep an eye out on the #giveaways channel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/3404373cc68def237d22e771f165a4abcfda85b9.png[/img]

[h1]Discount[/h1]

The game will also be on a 50% discount during this week, it's an anniversary deal. It's the biggest discount the game ever had, so if the game seemed to expensive before, now's your chance to get it cheaper in the case you don't win at the giveaway described above.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/995c8e4eade8ab76dc3f206ee8a35114461c85c8.png[/img]

[h1]The author of this post[/h1]

My name is SilviuShader, but everybody calls me Shader.

[img]https://c.tenor.com/A-PSSAJ9s9wAAAAd/giovanni-giorgio.gif[/img]

[h1]SVET[/h1]

This section has nothing to do with [i]PalmRide[/i], nor with the game that we are currently working on. The post pretty much ended with the previous paragraph.

[i]PalmRide[/i] benefited much from the help of [b]Taranasus[/b], who kept a link towards the [i]PalmRide[/i] Steam page inside [i]Vecter[/i] for almost a year. I think that link brought many [i]Vecter[/i] fans to [i]PalmRide[/i]. To those of you who are [i]Vecter[/i] fans, I want to let you know that [b]Taranasus[/b] is working on another game, [i]Super Vecter Elite Turbo[/i]. [url=https://www.youtube.com/c/TaranasusVideos]You might want to keep an eye out for that.[/url] I don't know how the game is gonna be, but I believe that it's going to be similar to the game with rockets we are currently making. 

Here's a video about the game:

[previewyoutube=BG-fdlEdGgA;full][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/7c564c0b7b2762998af7b58e2f86357ea8a0cb10.png[/img]

notes.title: PalmRide turns one month.
notes.content:
That's right, PalmRide was released on this day last month. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/3b846d9e92eb1bac86571236c30b68529d4dcda9.png[/img]

Since then, we tried to polish a few things that weren't quite right, and add some of the features you requested.

[b]The first month[/b]

When we released the game, we didn't know what to expect. This was our first game on Steam, so we had no experience with that. We were a bit pessimistic too, knowing that the games we published for Android didn't have many downloads. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/63cadee3cf879ad5a301c8a7ce30fc9c787c2163.png[/img]

After the first day of release, we had already received tons of positive feedback, and the downloads were going great. For that, we are deeply grateful. The rest of the month was good too, a lot of people tried the game and got some pretty good scores in the Rad Guy game mode. REPTONE got a score of over 80k, which is a lot more than us, the devs, can achieve.

Thank you for making the launch of the game a success!

[b]Giveaway[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/d8a98fa26468b567fb1548f430b0ce6a23c658bb.png[/img]

To celebrate this milestone, we'll be giving 3 keys for the game.
All you have to do is join our Discord server [url=https://discord.gg/NgZ3ygb8N5]https://discord.gg/NgZ3ygb8N5[/url] and keep an eye out for the giveaway in the #giveaway channel. The giveaway is set to begin at around 10AM PDT, but it may be delayed a bit/ it may start a bit earlier. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/fab0a083c9dd71d9c81fdcd6af68b5678b78f999.png[/img]

PLEASE DO NOT ATTEND THE GIVEAWAY IF YOU ALREADY HAVE THE GAME IN YOUR LIBRARY!!! (unless you want to give the key to a friend who can't buy the game)

[b]Patch notes[/b]

Since the last update, the game received a few minor updates. So here are the changes:

[list]
[*] Faster loading/ unloading times.
[*] Probably fixed some of the end game crashes.
[*] Added x64 support for PalmRide.
[*] Added horn.
[*] Fixed a bug when using the controller for the UI. 
[/list]

It's not much, but it's honest work.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/107bec38dbbe5254399b6b4115f9e7a55b8298e9.jpg[/img]

Keep in mind that since the last update, we started college, and we don't have that much time remaining for updates to the game. That is not to say that the game won't receive any further updates, in fact, we have some really cool things planned, and we'll reveal them eventually.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/942054d7fb65794fa43cce78445235cb93ef3905.png[/img]

[b]Dev.Play 2021[/b]

Dev.Play is coming back this year, and PalmRide is attending the event... again...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/b7f723b0b91b4838bead8957086e9dec1f432dec.png[/img]

The event will have dedicated page on Steam, which will be featured on the front page of Steam on October 25. On that page, there will be PalmRide too. We may add a discount to the game specifically for that event, so keep an eye out for that in case you want to buy the game cheaper.

This event is mainly focused on game developers and publishers, so I wouldn't suggest attending the event to see PalmRide there, because there will probably not be any livestreams with the game. We'll let you know if the event is worth attending for regular gamers, but as far as we know, the conference is dedicated to the devs. We'll have to dig a bit deeper into the details though.

[b]Thank you[/b]

Again, thanks for this first month of the game. We'll continue to bring (bigger or smaller) updates to the game, so keep an eye out for these updates.

Until next time, keep driving, and don't forget to shoot those motorcyclists.

notes.title: All-time leaderboard, CRT UI
notes.content:
Okay, this update is a small one.

[b]Patch notes:[/b]

[list]
[*] Hopefully fixed the crash when the game ends in Rad Guy game mode... again...
[*] There is now a leaderboard that doesn't reset daily. You can find it here: [url=https://www.palmride.online/leaderboards.html?table=radguy&type=alltime]https://www.palmride.online/leaderboards.html?table=radguy&type=alltime[/url]
[*] You can now choose if you want the CRT effect over the UI elements. Disabling the CRT effect on the UI may make reading text easier, while still having the CRT effect enabled for the rest of the game.
[/list]

[b]Next up?[/b]

Bug fixes and then controller support.

Thanks!

notes.title: Bug fixes, police vehicles tweaks, nitro, music, tweaks
notes.content:
[b]Patch Notes[/b]

[list]
[*] Fixed a memory leak related to the music (if not solved, this would've caused the game to frequently crash due to the high amount of memory that was used).
[*] The prior update introduced a new bug. When a default song ended, the music visualizer would disappear. This problem was solved in this update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/49baaf80c519fdf6e3135e0fb364678d10f795ba.png[/img]

[*] When you hit the "QUIT RIDE" button, the "life lost" sound is no longer played. It was a pretty minor bug, but now it's solved.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/a796547813b5aa6d3a4f6c99eba8a5d8ff6634f1.png[/img]

[*] On Firefox, the footer of the website would overlap with the text from episode 1. This was fixed.
[*] Replaced "getting" with "taking" in a sentence from episode 1.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/41ea1c27e7e9cde0b78014351595772f5498b2c3.png[/img]

[*] Tweaked police vehicles. Now they are easier to spot and avoid.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/6433182ea017d460a783b163ba857061f2609dda.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/f28bacc92c94b1ee302fb7bb21e9c8787663c2e9.gif[/img]

[*] To use NITRO you now have to HODL CTRL, instead of just pressing CTRL once and waiting to drain the nitro tank. This is how all driving games handle NITRO, so it would probably make sense for PalmRide to do the same.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/84988812a9ce0dcfe413a1e1e9fccd166f58c204.png[/img]

[*] You can now skip the current song while using custom music. You just have to press N on the keyboard, and it will play the next song.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/420e2dec4de1a303cb83da7eec6ccc047546feb1.png[/img]

[*] There is now a timer in the LEADERBOARD menu which shows how much time is left until the leaderboard resets. This one suggested by @Reptone from our Discord server.
[*] The player no longer shoots with bullets when you hit the "RESUME" button.
[/list]

[b]Next[/b]

The next things on the to-do list are some issues similar to the ones above. After that, we may make a global leaderboard (independent to the daily ones). This feature was requested by you, so it's worth trying to implement it.

Also, today I (Silviu, the lead dev of the game) bought an Xbox One controller. So, I may start implementing controller support really soon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/9c35d04ac18dfbb181836ea74dbcf8a4cd0f0aac.png[/img]

Initially I thought I was buying an Xbox One Series X controller, but apparently it's an Xbox One controller. It doesn't matter that much though, they are pretty much the same thing. One minor difference I noticed is that the Xbox One controller uses replaceable batteries, but that's a pretty minor inconvenience.

Alright, that's it for this update.
Thank you!

notes.title: EPISODE 1 IS OUT!
notes.content:
[b]What? You thought this game had no story?[/b]

You are wrong! We just released the first episode. 
You may read it here: [url=https://www.palmride.online/episode1.html]https://www.palmride.online/episode1.html[/url]

This story has been written by @DabuAlexandru from our Discord server, and polished by @COVALENT, the sound guy of the team.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/f9d85a92f137ca168e0c5965aaf8a0ffa271defc.png[/img]

[b]Patch notes[/b]

[list]

notes.title: Fixed demo bugs
notes.content:
So, it's been a while since I last made an update here.. I think the last update was for the demo release. Since then, a lot of you played the demo and gave me feedback which I very much appreciate, and I want to thank you for that.

[img]https://media1.giphy.com/media/l3q2wJsC23ikJg9xe/giphy.gif?cid=ecf05e47wdige8lvds5ldgl2jidtanwd27nvq2bkkk15bq8z&rid=giphy.gif[/img]

[b]Why were you so silent regarding the game since the demo was released?[/b]

Welp, the demo was launched right before I started the exams session at college. I had to study for the exams so I didn't really work much on the game (neither the artist and the composer did). I had the last exam a few days ago, so now I have some time to work on the game. 
I will start working on more game features but, some of you found bugs/ problems in the demo so I decided to fix them (though I haven't and won't fix all the problems you found, only the major ones for now, the others will be fixed in the final release of the game.... yes, I am talking about the death screen...).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/f7608fa82a3a47a0068fc53272edaf8a3c90f9ad.png[/img]

[b]Patch notes[/b]

[list]
[*] Fixed fullscreen errors when pressing alt+tab (just made the game borderless window fullscreen instead of classic fullscreen).
[*] Made road reflections look more realistic.
[*] Fixed options menu bug when you press the ESC key and the right UI panel doesn't disappear.
[*] Fixed UI bugs that happen when the window is not active.
[*] Added one more line near the edge of the roads.
[/list]

[b]What's next?[/b]

Well, while working on the demo I kinda wrote some terrible code so I could finish it faster, so I guess I will clean up that code, then continue working on demo fixes and features for the final game.

Thanks again for playing the demo and giving feedback! It really means a lot to me and the team. In fact, I didn't really expect so many downloads for the demo (there were more than 3000 downloads). It's the first time when a game that I've worked on is really played by people. For this, I am grateful. Also, some of you guys reacted and commented to the posts I made on social media related to PalmRide, when I was answering your questions I was feeling like: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/d650b90556c41a3dd96e6de044bc382486847248.jpg[/img]

Don't get me wrong, I like that you guys are interested, but I am really not used to this. Anyways, thanks guys!

notes.title: Reimplemented flight, better car animation (WIP)
notes.content:
[h1]Yep, it's exactly what the title says. [/h1]

[img]https://media2.giphy.com/media/kEuoboHo4QhbPzjit2/giphy.gif?cid=ecf05e47hm9pis6agv29y6s1p1bem8e5p8lgjb9x632nsss9&rid=giphy.gif[/img]

So... a bit of backstory... I originally implemented flight in the game a few months ago, and the idea was to fly over the cars and have different obstacles that you avoid when flying (like helicopters). This turned out to be not so fun (in fact it was really annoying), and you couldn't see the obstacles well. 

[h2]So now... CHANGE OF PLAN. [/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/63ac31ea907e9cb68139a542c04bfa3680eaa708.png[/img]

Instead of flying over a long distance, you would just fly over a small distance (this will help you avoid the cars for a couple of seconds without doing much). There will also be parts where the road is destroyed so you'll have to fly over that gap. At the moment, it looks something like this:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/4b34f16183c5bb89dae9267b5bc4397fad5b51f5.gif[/img]
Excuse the terrible framerate (Steam doesn't let me upload gifs that are larger). Also, please excuse the terrible car sprite when flying, we didn't fully change the car sprite in the game YET. Also, please excuse the terrible looking "palms zone".

Now, enough for the excuses, there are many possibilities for this flight mechanic (like flying over the sea and avoiding dolphins who jump high in the sky... was I high when I thought about this? No, COVALENT thought about this when HE was high)

[h1]The new car[/h1]

As I said in the previous update, we now got a new team member who is an artist. In the last update he started redrawing the car, and now it's pretty much drawn from all angles (instead of the angle for flight, and those for going uphill/ downhill).
Anyways, I think he has done an awesome job remaking the car so far. Just take a look at how smooth it seems when I turn the car:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/da8da7919711ed0e85adad6a76f6a58cad348a97.gif[/img]
VEEEEERY SMOOOOOOTH (again, excuse the low framerate of the gif... damn you Steam)
It's not obvious from this gif (because I don't use the brakes), but now, when you press the brakes, the stop lights start flickering... but again... WHO USES THE BRAKES? they only slow you down...

[h1]Yep, I think that was it[/h1]

I once again apologize for the slow progress, it's all because of the d**n college. Luckily the winter holiday is coming soon, and hopefully I'll be able to get more work done. Also, this is not all that has been implemented into the game since the last update. I also started working on the leaderboard system (and it's pretty much done, I just have to work some more on the security of the server), and fixed/ polished things in general.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/0d4b6e205c557bf94bd310c49075edcd27f54781.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/8561a90478bd22075e943cccc322a1664c042fbb.png[/img]

[h1]All right, now that's all, cheers fellow Palm Riders (I meant Realm Spiders)![/h1]

notes.title: New game zone, passages, new team member
notes.content:
First of all, hi guys! Instead of excusing myself for the slow progress and updates (because you know the story... homework for college), I will go straight and show you the progress that has been made since our last encounter.

[h1]New game zone[/h1]
Ok, this zone has been in the game for quite a while, but now I want to officially tell you about it (even though it is present in the first trailer of the game). It's the "palm zone", a game zone meant to give kind of a GTA Vice City vibe, something like an drive near the beach or something like that.
Right now it looks something like this:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/ccf1ac33e27b82623725ffbd90cf546a0d11e16a.png[/img]

Because I mentioned GTA Vice City... here's an accurate representation of what PalmRide really is:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/434897b7ddba8b614b5f41559895bb598d27febd.png[/img]

The first thing you may notice is that there is a different car sprite (again, I know). It is still work in progress and it's made by our new team member. That's right, we are now 3 guys (one programmer, one artist and one sound guy). You may also notice there is inconsistency in the colors.. that's because some colors were used in the previous version of the zone, and now it's having a reskin.. so... inconsistency in colors.

[h1]Passages[/h1]
I recently player Lotus III and I noticed that there are passages... so I started implementing passages in PalmRide too.. here's what I'm talking about:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/e7b9436c60b392c2876e4ad7b51305993a46d533.png[/img]

Aaand I think that's pretty much it.... 

Oh wait, there is still one thing I missed. There will be "THE STEAM GAME FESTIVAL SOON" and we want to attend it.. somehow. And for this, we need to have a demo of the game on Steam... so... DEMO COMING SOON. 
The demo will feature only the CITY in singleplayer mode. (yes, this indeed means there will be an online daily ranking system in the final game... LET THE BEST PLAYER BE FIRST)

For this the ranking system I mentioned before I will need a database, so here's what I'll do:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/6ecbbe3f4bf82b5df247f60111a15ad30ae0c3c6.png[/img]

Yep, this drake meme is the only one I know works in any situation.. so.. take it or leave it.

As a side note, I kinda am a teacher right now (though I am not paid). I teach some students assembly programming the help them pass the exam. If you guys (students) are reading this, please ping me :). You may ask: what? this is why the game progress is so slow... well.. partly... I think I spend more time working on the game than teaching so.. this shouldn't be much of a problem.
You may ask, how do I teach to students, well.. like this:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38713185/002a93502b6713a777caa7e5a522b35b16ae2d8a.png[/img]


That has been it. Keep being awesome, guys :)
